title: Event Log Mapping Playbook (v0.7 exploratory)
body:
Purpose:
This playbook captures a working approach to mapping runtime events into a compact, SIEM-friendly audit log schema and to surface a minimal evidence set for automated compliance workflows. It is intentionally pragmatic: close-to-runtime fields, conservative growth of the schema, and clear migration steps.

Context & constraints (quick):
- Need one canonical event model used by hosted API, Dedicated control plane, and Private deployment tooling.
- RBAC v2 introduces resource-scoped roles and ephemeral role bindings; logs must record enough to reconstruct authorization decisions without leaking PII.
- SIEM exports should align with common ECS-like conventions to ease ingestion by Splunk/Elastic/QRadar.
- Evidence automation (for audits) will pull a deterministic subset of fields per event-class.

Scope for this doc:
- Event naming conventions, core field set, severity mapping, and basic SIEM export map.
- RBAC v2 field guidance (what to log vs what to redact).
- Versioning and migration strategy v0.7 -> v1.0 candidate steps.
- Implementation checklist and open questions.

1) Event naming and taxonomy (short):
- Use dotted, lower-case nouns: auth.login.success, auth.login.failure, resource.access.denied, model.request.start, model.request.complete, model.fallback.
- Prefixes: auth.*, resource.*, model.*, deployment.*, system.*. Keep verbs to the rightmost segment.
- Event families should be broad; fine-grain detail lives in attributes map to keep index cost predictable.

2) Core audit schema (flat, SIEM-friendly):
- event_id: unique UUID for the event (string)
- event_ts: ISO8601 UTC timestamp (string)
- event_type: taxonomy name (string)
- severity: info|notice|warning|error|critical (string)
- outcome: success|failure|unknown (string)
- actor_id: opaque user id (redactable) (string)
- actor_role_ids: list of role ids applied during decision (list of strings)
- actor_role_names: OPTIONAL human-friendly names, redaction recommended in high-sensitivity customers (string)
- resource_type: e.g., model, dataset, project (string)
- resource_id: canonical resource identifier (string)
- request_id: request correlation id (string)
- service: product surface (hosted-api|dedicated|private-controlplane) (string)
- host_region: region tag (string)
- client_ip: IP or proxy tag (redact per policy) (string)
- user_agent: client user-agent (string)
- duration_ms: numeric-ish as string for indexing (string)
- payload_summary: small JSON blob-as-string summarizing request (trim to 1024 chars) (string)
- error_code: canonical error code if any (string)
- linked_evidence_ids: list of evidence artifact ids (list of strings)
- schema_version: semantic-ish v0.7 (string)

Notes: keep top-level fields flat. Extra diagnostic detail should be stored in an attached evidence artifact rather than in the main event body to reduce event size.

3) Event severity & outcome mapping guidance (examples):
- auth.login.failure: severity=warning, outcome=failure
- auth.login.success: severity=info, outcome=success
- model.request.start: severity=info, outcome=unknown
- model.request.complete (with fallback): severity=notice, outcome=success and set attribute fallback=true
- model.request.error (OOM, inference failure): severity=error, outcome=failure, attach stacktrace evidence id

4) SIEM export mapping (ECS-like suggested fields)
Purpose: a straightforward one-to-one mapping to accelerate ingestion. We recommend shipping both the raw event and the mapped ECS envelope. Minimal mapping:
- ecs.timestamp <- event_ts
- ecs.event.id <- event_id
- ecs.event.type <- event_type
- ecs.event.outcome <- outcome
- ecs.event.severity <- severity
- ecs.user.id <- actor_id
- ecs.user.name <- actor_role_names (only if permitted)
- ecs.network.client.ip <- client_ip (apply redaction rule)
- ecs.url.path <- resource_id (when resource is an API endpoint)
- ecs.service.name <- service
- ecs.duration.ms <- duration_ms
- ecs.stack_trace <- error evidence artifact (link)

Implementation note: produce a lightweight flattened ECS view for high-throughput consumers and store the full raw event for internal investigations.

5) RBAC v2 considerations (what to log):
- Log role ids and the binding id used for the decision. Role bindings are often ephemeral; record binding_ts to make the audit reconstructable.
- DO NOT log token values, full credentials, or private keys. Replace with token_hash if needed for correlation.
- For high-sensitivity customers (HIPAA/PII), default to recording role ids only, not role names. Provide a retrieval API (audit-only) to resolve role names via require-auth.
- Record policy version or policy-check-id to tie a decision to a policy revision.

6) Evidence automation (how events trigger evidence collection):
- Evidence levels: minimal, diagnostic, full. Each event_type maps to a required evidence level. Example mapping:
  - auth.login.failure -> minimal (auth headers sans tokens, timestamp, actor_id) + diagnostic on repeated failures
  - model.request.error -> diagnostic (request payload summary + model logs + stack trace)
  - deployment.rollout.failed -> full (deployment manifest, rollout diff, operator id)
- Evidence artifacts should be stored in a tamper-evident store (S3 versioned + KMS + immutable tags) and referenced by linked_evidence_ids.
- Evidence TTLs: evidence level drives retention class. Minimal: 90d; Diagnostic: 365d; Full: 7 years (enterprise customers may override).

7) Schema versioning and migration strategy (v0.7 -> v1.0):
- Semantic intent: vX.Y where X increments for breaking changes, Y for additive backwards-compatible fields. v0.7 is exploratory. v1.0 freeze planned when: RBAC v2 fields approved, evidence taxonomy stabilized, and SIEM mapping vetted by 2 customers.
- Backwards compatibility rules: always accept older schema_version values when reading. New fields must be optional and default to null/empty.
- Migration steps:
  1) Deploy ingestion that accepts both v0.7 and v1.0.
  2) Start emitting v0.8 with authoritative actor_role_ids list and binding_id.
  3) After 60 days of dual-emit, flip default to v1.0.
  4) Deprecate old fields with 90-day notice and maintain a translation layer for SIEM exports.

8) Performance & cost tradeoffs (practical):
- Keep event payload < 2KiB for high-traffic endpoints. Move large artifacts to evidence store.
- Index only the small subset of fields used in SLOs/alerts (event_ts, event_type, actor_id, outcome, severity).
- Batch-export to SIEM — use compressed NDJSON and incremental checkpoints.

9) Implementation checklist (short-term work items):
- [ ] Add schema_version to all event emitters (API surface, runtime, control plane).
- [ ] Implement actor_role_ids logging in auth middleware and include binding_id.
- [ ] Build evidence artifact API with put/get and immutability markers.
- [ ] Produce an ECS-mapped export transformer and integration test with SIEM partner.
- [ ] Draft RBAC v2 logging policy for customers (redaction defaults).
- [ ] Run load test on event sizes and SIEM export throughput.

10) Open questions / unresolved decisions (for sync):
- Should we include anonymous session tags (session_id) by default for model requests? Pros: easier correlation. Cons: increases PII surface.
- How aggressively do we redact user_agent and client_ip for on-prem customers vs hosted? Policy needed.
- Do we require immutable storage for evidence by default or opt-in per customer?

Appendix: Example event (flattened v0.7)
{"event_id":"6f7a8e2c-3b2a-4b0a-9c45-1a2b3c4d5e6f","event_ts":"2024-09-16T17:03:21Z","event_type":"model.request.complete","severity":"notice","outcome":"success","actor_id":"usr_8a3f","actor_role_ids":["role:reader:project-123"],"resource_type":"model","resource_id":"m:gpt-xxl:2024-09-10","request_id":"req_0019","service":"hosted-api","host_region":"us-west-2","duration_ms":"211","payload_summary":"prompt_length=532,answer_tokens=120","linked_evidence_ids":["evid_20240916_0001"],"schema_version":"v0.7"}

------
Notes to self: add suggested log size limits to SDK docs; coordinate with SRE on batching defaults. Come back to archive policy for evidence TTLs with legal.

End of playbook (work-in-progress).
